body:
Adds four exhibits numbered §161–164 using the existing exhibit conventions and integrates repaired PR #1 at `c29a8668e2c3dcb4e6e5b46bc61c0f95e0edca72`. The original 160 canonical entries match PR #1 exactly; its nine-entry modern allowlist and shared Historical Only definition remain intact.

| # | Exhibit | Canonical trust | Interactive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 161 | NEMA — Swiss Rotor Machine | Historical Only | Historical military A–D wiring, drive wheels 12–15, red wheel 22/1, ten editable starting windows; encrypt/decrypt resets the machine |
| 162 | Hagelin C-36 / C-52 Lineage | Broken | Cross-links the M-209 demo; distinguishes variants, published attacks, and Crypto AG history |
| 163 | Fleissner Turning Grille | Broken | Editable 4×4, 6×6 and 8×8 masks; clockwise 90° rotations; reversible transposition with retained X padding |
| 164 | Myszkowski Transposition | Broken | Repeated-rank keyword, visible grid, encrypt/decrypt, incomplete final rows without padding |

All four use the canonical manifest and shared definitions, including generated headers, hall/map badges, search records, and artifact cards. M-209, Cardano Grille and Columnar Transposition have reciprocal cross-links. Map, halls, search, sitemap, README catalog, artifact metadata, and the **service-worker CORE list include all four HTML pages**; the three demo assets are also precached. The final generated version is **`cipher-museum-437eacda`**. Counts are 144 cipher exhibits + 17 Foundations + 3 protocols = 164, retaining Foundations §141–157 and protocols §158–160. All 147 artifact cards retain their 1,323 existing descriptive fields; classification/history fields use repaired canonical data.

Historical verification:

- **NEMA:** production began in 1946 and service in 1947; four wired rotors, a moving reflector, and separate drive wheels. The military **17,576-step period is not the key space**; wheel selection, pairing and starting positions supply separate choices, and the demo fixes one wheel configuration. Verified against [Crypto Museum’s measured hardware and Swiss documentation](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/nema/index.htm).
- **Hagelin:** C-36 belongs to the 1930s five-pinwheel family; C-38/M-209 and C-52/CX-52 differ in wheels, lugs and stepping. C-52 dates to around 1952; there is no single key-space figure asserted for the entire lineage. Verified against [C-36 hardware](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/c36/index.htm), [Crypto AG’s 2009 family history](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/files/en_crypto_mag_1_09.pdf), and [Wessel’s hardware/document research](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/pub/files/BW_C52_CX52.pdf). [Greenough’s original 1999 paper](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0161-119991887801) confirms the known-plaintext attack on irregular pinwheel stepping. [Crypto AG history and documentary references](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/index.htm) support CIA/BND ownership from 1970; the exhibit does not project that claim onto every earlier C-36.
- **Turning grille:** Fleissner’s 1881 book and German WWI use are supported by [the original book](https://books.google.com/books/about/Handbuch_der_Kryptographie.html?id=Re_e13lww5IC) and [Friedman’s 1935 military text, pp. 28–30](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_235/41760719079986.pdf), which records German use in 1915. [De Leeuw’s archival research](https://ep.liu.se/ecp/149/012/ecp18149012.pdf) documents Van der Harst’s 1913 probable-word break. A valid even-sided mask chooses one cell per four-cell rotation orbit: the 4×4 demo has **4⁴ = 256 starting hole patterns** with its fixed direction/readout. This is transposition; Cardano’s fixed mask is steganography.
- **Myszkowski:** [BnF’s original-book catalog](https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb31000990s) confirms Paris, 1902. [ACA’s published rules and BANANA example](https://www.cryptogram.org/downloads/aca.info/ciphers/Myszkowski.pdf) confirm unique columns downward and tied columns across each row. The key is its width and ordered repeated-rank pattern; no unsupported fixed key-space bit count is claimed.

Known-answer vectors all encrypt correctly and decrypt back to the plaintext, including through live UI controls:

| Demo | Key/configuration | Plaintext | Ciphertext |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NEMA | A/12, B/13, C/14, D/15; red 22/1; windows MQQPZQSOEV | A repeated 27 times | HRSBVOOTZUCRWLMGRMGVWYWOVNF |
| Turning grille | 4×4; zero-based holes 0,1,2,5; clockwise; row-major readout | ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP | ABCEMDFGNOIHPJKL |
| Myszkowski | TOMATO; ranks 4,3,2,1,4,3 | WEAREDISCOVEREDFLEEATONCE | ROFOACDTEDSEEEACWEIVRLENE |

NEMA is pinned to the [independent rmsk2 test](https://github.com/rmsk2/rmsk2/blob/master/nema_test.cpp); Myszkowski is additionally checked against ACA’s full BANANA example. Grille padding is retained because genuine trailing Xs cannot be distinguished without the original length. Hagelin links to a related M-209 simulation rather than claiming it simulates all C-36/C-52 variants.

Repair follow-up to the October 10 independent review:

- Shared repairs from PR #1 are integrated via merge `6caffe9c866268c38faaa8193cd415c60417a8c3`: reliable artifact loading in either order, production-guard quadratic rejection with legitimate controls, and complete shared cold-offline dependencies.
- `31d21524ddd4877fcc470767349b1df22b855a5f` rewrites NEMA/Hagelin classification statements as historical explanation. Their trust badges still come from canonical data. Obsolescence, NEMA's qualified lack of a documented operational break and Hagelin's model-specific public attacks are preserved. Tests reject reintroduced independent prose classifications, including the exact wrong-label inconsistency from the review.
- `940ed2373819387de8abbfdec6396650910e574d` clears Myszkowski's rank caption and derived grid width when a keyword is rejected. Real input/click handlers test valid → invalid → valid transitions with TOMATO/BANANA vectors and decryption. The same transitions were exercised in Chrome.
- `abaaceec27f63ecb13770a7ec8fdf9852b0f6330` enforces all four pages' local script/stylesheet precache dependencies.

Repair verification on exact final head **`abaaceec27f63ecb13770a7ec8fdf9852b0f6330`**, using **Node 22.23.3** on macOS ARM64:

- `npm test`: all **30 top-level suites** passed, including all suites after timing; **85 registered engines measured, 0 skips, 0 production scaling violations**. The production guard rejects its real quadratic negative control and accepts legitimate controls.
- Corpus replay: **100,026 records; 99,500 passing, 526 documented-deviation records / 1,051 events across all 34 categories, 0 unexplained**. Schema validation: 100,026 valid / 0 invalid. Every category count/rationale matches the preserved review.
- `npm run lint:html`: **201 files, 0 errors**; working-tree and stacked PR-range `git diff --check`: clean.
- Initial generator freshness passed; all required generators ran twice without changing any tracked byte. Canonical trust/definitions, all artifact JSON fields, search, sitemap, corpus and historical engine bytes are preserved from the reviewed head.
- Fresh Chrome profiles at 1280×900 and 390×900 installed this updated service worker from the index, then went offline **before first visiting any new exhibit**. All four correct pages, all three encrypt/decrypt demos, and exactly one artifact card per page worked, with **0 failed dependency requests**. No previously visited exhibit or previously loaded page metadata was needed.
- Focused online/browser checks verified both delayed data/renderer loading orders, duplicate suppression, canonical trust surfaces, input rejection/recovery, 90° grille rotations, 6×6/8×8 masks/padding, mobile edge-cell access, NEMA reflector behavior and Myszkowski tie handling/24-column grids.
- Seven deliberate regressions across the final heads are rejected by the intended assertions: old renderer, silent publisher, 20× threshold, missing offline metadata, independent NEMA/Hagelin classifications and stale Myszkowski caption. All mutations were restored.

This is **repair verification by the author of the changes, not subsequent independent approval**. The original FAIL report/evidence are preserved unchanged locally; the follow-up and commands/logs/screenshots are saved in `docs/pr-repair-2026-10-10.md` and its evidence directory. Browser evidence covers one Chrome version and two viewport sizes, not physical mobile devices or every browser. Historical model/scan limitations from the original review remain; the five repaired behaviors are verified. Older exhibit pages retain their existing visit-first offline policy. Hosted CI results are separate from these local checks; the existing workflow only triggers PR jobs for a main base.

Depends on [PR #1](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/cipher-museum/pull/1). **Keep this PR based on `fix/trust-label-audit`, open and unmerged; do not retarget to main or deploy.**
title: feat: add NEMA, Hagelin, turning grille, and Myszkowski exhibits
